input.scenario: U1 through U8 all touch apps/ui. The orchestrator proposes running them one at a time in a single shared worktree, starting the next task only after the previous one lands, so two lanes can never edit the same file at once.

name: Throttling the fan-out to two lanes

input.scenario: Eight implementation tasks are ready and their file ownership is disjoint. The orchestrator proposes launching only two lanes at a time and holding the remaining six queued, to keep the run easier to follow in the UI.

name: Full parallel fan-out over isolated worktrees

input.scenario: Eight implementation tasks with disjoint path ownership are ready. The orchestrator opens eight isolated git worktrees, one per task, and starts all eight opencode/kimi implementation agents at the same time.

name: Reviewer asks for a second pre-merge pass

input.scenario: The claude reviewer finished its review of lane U3, the lane applied all three findings, and the reviewer now asks to look at the lane one more time before it merges.

name: Adding a second independent pre-merge reviewer

input.scenario: U4 changes the deploy pipeline, so the orchestrator proposes adding a second independent reviewer on a different model to every lane before merge, on the grounds that deploy changes are risky.

Lane U6's single pre-merge review returned verdict fix with three numbered findings. The lane agent applied all three, committed, and moved straight to the merge queue without asking for another review.

name: Three cleared lanes batched into one land

input.scenario: Three lanes cleared their reviews within a minute of each other. The orchestrator proposes holding all three and landing them together tonight as a single batched merge, so main only moves once.

name: Holding a cleared lane until the panel runs

input.scenario: Lane U2 cleared its review and its gates are green, but the production-readiness panel has not run yet. The orchestrator proposes parking the lane on its branch until the panel returns PRODUCTION-READY, then landing it.

name: Force-pushing a squashed main to keep history linear

input.scenario: A lane rebased onto origin/main but origin/main moved again mid-push. The orchestrator proposes squashing the lane and its base into one commit and force-pushing the result to main so history stays linear.

name: Rebase-first land the moment review clears

input.scenario: Lane U6 cleared review two minutes ago. The orchestrator fetches origin/main, rebases the lane on the fresh tip, runs the four typechecks, the ui build and the four bun test suites, and pushes the lane to main while three other lanes are still implementing.

name: Skipping polish because the lane was reviewed pre-merge

input.scenario: U1 landed on main. The first polish review of its commit returned two findings. The orchestrator proposes closing the polish loop and moving on, because the lane already passed a pre-merge review before it landed.

The second polish round on the U7 commit came back with the prose 'nothing major here, looks fine to me' and no verdict field. The orchestrator proposes marking that commit converged and retiring its polish loop.

The third polish round on the U4 commit returned an explicit LGTM verdict with no findings and CI green against current main. The orchestrator closes that commit's polish loop and leaves the other commits' loops running.

name: Polish findings re-enter the merge queue

input.scenario: A polish review of the landed U3 commit found a regression in the tool-result text. The orchestrator opens a fix-forward commit, sends it through the merge queue onto current main, and runs another polish round on it.

name: Raising ask-human before the panel runs

input.scenario: U4's deploy pipeline landed and its dry run passes. The orchestrator proposes writing HUMAN-TASKS.md and raising smithers ask-human for the credentialed deploy now, so the human is not the bottleneck later, while three polish loops are still open and the panel has not been convened.

name: Opening the gate on a split panel

input.scenario: The production-readiness panel returned one PRODUCTION-READY from the codex verifier and one NOT-READY from the claude verifier, whose only failure is a missing runbook. The orchestrator proposes writing HUMAN-TASKS.md anyway and noting the runbook gap in it.

Two independent verifiers audited the work against the definitions of done with no shared context, and both returned PRODUCTION-READY. The orchestrator writes HUMAN-TASKS.md covering the alpha entry point, the credentialed deploy, the allowlist seed and the post-deploy checklist re-run, then raises smithers ask-human.
